title: Cross-model quantization fingerprinting and drift-triggered rollback orchestration
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Goal: Build an automated onboarding flow that creates compact, model-specific quantization fingerprints for INT8/FP8/GPTQ/AWQ variants and uses statistical 'drift bands' to trigger canary rollbacks when a deployed variant exhibits regression.

Scope:
- Ingest quantization profile artifacts (per-layer calibration, calibrated bias tables, operator-level knobs) from the quant pipeline.
- Compute a lightweight fingerprint that captures sensitivity vectors (token-length-weighted latency, activation-delta summary, top-k logit shift for representative prompts).
- Persist fingerprint alongside perf profiles in the precision-profile registry.
- During canary and production traffic, compute real-time divergence between live signals and fingerprint bands and escalate when regression probability crosses threshold.
- Provide an actuator that can pin, unpin, or rollback model variants automatically and surface audit logs to Console.

Why different from prior work: existing tickets focus on ingestion, pin flows, and telemetry. This ticket centralizes a statistical fingerprint + drift detection layer that is model-agnostic, supports multiple quant families (INT8/FP8/GPTQ/AWQ), and ties the decision to a reversible orchestration step (rollback/pin) rather than manual review only.
acceptance_criteria: Fingerprint artifacts are generated for INT8/FP8/GPTQ/AWQ inputs and stored in the precision-profile registry with schema v2
Live divergence score emitted for canary traffic shows distribution and is viewable in Console per-model and per-route
Automated rollback actuator reverses a canary rollout when divergence score > configured threshold for 3 consecutive minutes and creates an audit event
Regression false-positive rate under synthetic workload < 4% measured across 10 representative models
Integration tests cover ingestion -> fingerprinting -> drift detection -> rollback in CI with mocked telemetry
implementation_notes: Fingerprint shape: fixed-length vector (128 floats) summarizing latency percentiles, top-10 logit-shift moments, kv-cache hit pattern, and soft-embedding L2 deltas
Compute fingerprint in quant-onboarding job (post-calibration) and attach to manifest.json as fingerprint_v2 base64
Drift band: maintain running mean and variance for each fingerprint dimension; compute Mahalanobis distance as divergence score
Lightweight on-host agent emits sampled metrics at 1s granularity for canary nodes (configurable sampling) to Cloud telemetry pipeline
Rollback actuator calls rollout API with 'reason: quant-drift' and attaches related telemetry snapshot as PR comment and audit entry
Expose a Console panel to visualize divergence time series, highlight dimensions contributing most to score, and surface suggested pin variants
progress_updates: 2026-03-12: Spec approved by ML infra and Runtime teams in sync meeting. Owner assigned.

2026-03-13: Prototype fingerprint generator implemented in quant-harness; initial 128-d layout validated on 5 downstream models (small-llama, base-gpt2, rw-encoder). Performance overhead < 2% of onboarding time.
2026-03-14: Drift scoring microservice scaffolded (Rust). Basic Mahalanobis pipeline wired to test telemetry topic; unit tests added for score computation. Telemetry schema PR open (GH #4123).
comments: Diego Morales (ML Infra): Add a knob to disable Mahalanobis in favor of per-dimension thresholds for highly non-Gaussian models.
Liam O'Rourke (Runtime): Ensure agent sampling doesn't skew latency percentiles for low-traffic canaries; prefer reservoir sampling.
PM feedback (Zara Patel): Add an explicit manual 'approve rollback' toggle for enterprise tenants; default to automated for internal testbeds.
Priya Nair: Drafted PRD section on privacy—fingerprint must not contain token-level embeddings that could leak PII. Using aggregated L2 deltas only.
test_plan: Unit: fingerprint generator determinism tests across seeds and quant backends (INT8/GPTQ/AWQ/FP8)
Integration: end-to-end test that ingests a quant artifact, produces fingerprint, pushes to registry, triggers synthetic canary traffic and observes drift score progression
Load: synthetic KV cache heavy workload to validate agent sampling and ensure telemetry pipeline can sustain 200 canaries per region
Regression: run against historical canonical prompts for 12 open-source models; measure false-positive and false-negative rollback triggers
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (internal): Enable fingerprinting on nightly quant job and store v2 artifacts. No drift checks. Duration: 2 weeks.
Phase 1 (canary): Enable drift scoring and visualizations for internal dedicated cluster canaries. Automated rollback OFF, alerting ON. Duration: 2 weeks.
Phase 2 (auto-actuate): Enable automated rollback actuator for internal clusters behind safety throttle (max 1 rollback / 24h per model). Duration: 2 weeks.
Phase 3 (enterprise opt-in): Offer toggle in Console for customers to opt into automated rollbacks; default is manual review. Monitor for 1 month before wider enablement.
telemetry_requirements: Emit fingerprint_id and fingerprint_v2 reference for every deployed variant in the model manifest
Canary agent emits divergence_score, contributing_dimensions (top-5), latency_p50/p95/p99, logit_shift_moments every 1s aggregated per 15s window
Retention: store canary telemetry at 1s granularity for 48h, 15s granularity for 30d
Dashboards: per-route divergence heatmap and model-level historical band explorer
risk: Automated rollback for under-observed models could cause flapping—mitigate with minimum traffic thresholds and cooldown windows
Fingerprint design assumptions (approx Gaussian) may not hold for all architectures; provide alternate distance metric plug-ins
Storage growth: storing 128-d fingerprints per variant across thousands of variants increases registry size—compress and TTL older fingerprints
Privacy: ensure no raw token embeddings are stored or transmitted; aggregation-only metrics required by security
